name: Shoko Relay
overview: Subtitle suffix renaming test build of Shoko Relay. Uses the existing Shoko Relay configuration.

releases.release_notes:
Subtitle naming is now configured only in `preferences.json`, keeping the original upstream settings page.

- Existing `Advanced.SubtitleRenameRules` remain compatible and preserve their ordered source-selection policy.
- New `Advanced.SubtitleFormatPreference` defaults to `["ass", "ssa", "srt", "vtt", "smi"]`. Set it to `["srt"]` to prefer SRT, followed by the other supported formats in their default order.
- Preferences accept up to ten distinct supported extensions, each containing one to ten ASCII letters or digits. Case, surrounding whitespace, and one leading dot are normalized; invalid, unsupported, and duplicate entries are ignored.
- The complete editor, preview, autosave, and drag ordering are preserved in the annotated `subtitle-rename-ui-v1` tag for future work.

Edit these fields inside the existing `Advanced` object, reload any open dashboard, and refresh the affected VFS paths. Original subtitle files remain untouched. The testing build keeps the existing plugin UUID and configuration location.

Validation: 63 tests passed locally, including physical mixed-case filenames and symlink refreshes. Release CI reruns the tests before packaging Linux ARM64, Linux x64, and Windows x64.

Fix the subtitle rule insertion marker changing position and brightness while dragging across the same gap. Both approaches now show a 3px line centered in the gap at full opacity; only the dragged row contents fade.

This is a CSS fix. Rule selection, reordering, automatic saving, and the configuration format are unchanged. The regression check covers both sides of the gap next to the dragged row.

Update from the subtitle testing repository, select and pin v0.17.4-dev.1003, and restart Shoko. Force-reload the ShokoRelay dashboard to load the updated CSS.

Feature commit: 38d5496. The fix originates on subtitle-rename and is merged into subtitle-rename-testing; testing repository and publishing changes remain confined to the testing branch.

Subtitle suffix rules now have three-line drag handles. Drag a handle above or below another row to change priority; the order saves when dropped. The existing Move up and Move down buttons remain available for keyboard use and touch browsers without native drag support.

The editor uses the existing validation, automatic saving, retry, and preview behavior. Subtitle selection and the configuration format are unchanged.

Update from the subtitle testing repository, select and pin v0.17.4-dev.1002, and restart Shoko. Force-reload the ShokoRelay dashboard to load the updated JavaScript, CSS, and icons.

Feature commit: 0e14ff4. This release includes feature changes from subtitle-rename; testing repository and release changes remain confined to subtitle-rename-testing.

Experimental ShokoRelay build adding ordered subtitle suffix rules to the VFS. Rules can map one subtitle to several output suffixes, preserve existing final suffixes, and resolve competing sources by row order and subtitle format.

Built from `subtitle-rename-testing`, incorporating feature commit `4d79596`. Testing manifest and publishing changes stay on this branch; `subtitle-rename` remains the upstream feature branch.

Packages target Linux ARM64, Linux x64, and Windows x64. Requires a compatible Shoko 6 daily build with .NET 10; the plugin references Shoko.Abstractions 6.0.0-alpha.84. The release workflow runs the test suite before publishing archives and updates the feed after all platforms succeed.

Add this repository manifest in Shoko:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/leo-maxwell/ShokoRelay/subtitle-rename-testing/manifest.json

The test version keeps the official plugin identity and uses the same configuration and Plex token. Back up the complete active configuration directory first. Keep official v0.17.3 installed for rollback, enable and pin this test version, restart Shoko, and force-reload the dashboard. If disabling the old version manually, do that before enabling the test version. Do not purge the shared configuration.

Start with preview and a filtered VFS refresh on a small series. Verify subtitle selection and playback in Plex before expanding the test. See [testing instructions](https://github.com/leo-maxwell/ShokoRelay/blob/subtitle-rename-testing/Docs/Testing.md).
